full_name: Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows
summary: Capacity plus time windows. Travel time equals Euclidean distance with no vehicle speed; a vehicle may arrive early and wait, but must not arrive after a customer's due time. The depot may always be returned to, which is what keeps the rollout from deadlocking.

constraints.name: Capacity
constraints.rule: the served load of a route must never exceed the vehicle capacity

constraints.name: Time Windows
constraints.rule: the arrival time at a customer must be <= due; arriving before ready is legal and the vehicle waits

constraints.name: Visit
constraints.rule: every customer is served exactly once

constraints.name: Depot
constraints.rule: every route starts and ends at the depot (node 0)

state_variables.name: current_time
state_variables.update: current_time = max(arrival, ready) + service_time; reset to 0 when a route returns to the depot
state_variables.reason: time-window feasibility depends on when the vehicle can start service, not only on distance

state_variables.name: time_windows
state_variables.reason: the [ready, due] pair of every node; index 0 is the depot with window [0, horizon]

state_variables.name: service_times
state_variables.reason: service at a customer consumes time before the next leg

masking_rules.name: visited_mask
masking_rules.condition: the customer has already been served

masking_rules.name: depot_always_allowed
masking_rules.condition: returning to the depot is legal in every state; it ends the current route
masking_rules.exception: this rule exists so that a customer whose window has closed can never make the state unsolvable

masking_rules.name: finished_mask
masking_rules.condition: all customers have been served; only the depot remains selectable

feasibility_checklist: every customer id 1..n appears exactly once across all routes
each route starts and ends at node 0
no route load exceeds the instance capacity
arrival at each customer is <= its due time, with early arrival allowed to wait
the reported cost equals the recomputed sum of Euclidean leg lengths
output_contract: the initial process is successful, the initial cost is {cost}
the process is successful, the best cost is {cost}

pomo_modification_plan.change: add an instance loader plus time-window and service-time generation for random training instances
pomo_modification_plan.why: the environment needs these tensors at reset time

pomo_modification_plan.change: accept time_windows and service_times and store them alongside depot_node_xy
pomo_modification_plan.why: everything downstream reads them from the environment

pomo_modification_plan.change: add the time-window mask and keep the depot unmasked
pomo_modification_plan.why: this is where constraints become legal actions

pomo_modification_plan.change: advance current_time and reset it on depot returns
pomo_modification_plan.why: the next mask depends on the updated time

pomo_modification_plan.change: concatenate current_time and window slack into the decoder context
pomo_modification_plan.why: the policy must see time to act on it, and the encoder input must not change

checkpoint_compatibility.risk: feeding time features into the encoder changes its input width and makes every encoder weight unloadable

run_plan.action: adapt the problem definition to CVRPTW: demands plus a [ready, due] window and a service time per customer
carry the clock and the windows through the environment and mask every customer whose window can no longer be met
keep the encoder input at the two coordinates and let the new state enter the decoder context
make the entry program load the instance, run the rollouts and print both contract lines
confirm the acceptance lines print on a real instance
run_plan.expect: the process is successful, the best cost is <float>

open_questions: whether the baseline checkpoint's decoder context width must change, which would leave exactly one layer randomly initialised
